title: WHOWAS: a persisted nick history, if it is wanted
description:
A persisted nick history is the only thing that can answer the security story
bead mimid-1wgh.140.3 opened with: a user who remembers talking to a nick in
their client's scrollback deserves to know which MIMI user URI that nick stood
for, even when the scrollback is older than the daemon run.

WHY THE IN-MEMORY ANSWER CANNOT DO IT. Within one run nothing is ever removed
from `Names`: `take_nick` (crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/names.rs) only ever
inserts, so a nick's meaning is fixed from the moment it is given. The one
place a nick changes meaning is `Names::load` at startup, when a kept
`ext["irc"]["nick"]` is malformed or was taken first and the nick is given
again, possibly to another user. That is across runs, and the in-memory times
die with the run, so WHOWAS can only ever say "known here since", never "used
to mean".

WHERE IT WOULD HAVE TO LIVE. Not a table of its own in mimid-agent-store:
AGENTS.md's crate map forbids that crate holding front-end types "except as
JSON in a record's per-front-end `ext` map". So the history belongs in
`ext["irc"]` on the `Person` record that already holds the user URI and the
current nick: the new data is the historical dimension (the nicks this person
had before, with when each was given and given up), not a new category of
contact record.

WHAT IT COSTS, and why Mark decides rather than an agent. A persisted history
outlives the client that saw the nick and becomes a durable record of whom the
user has talked to, which is a new thing to protect and a new thing to expire.
It needs a retention policy and a way to drop it. Bead mimid-1wgh.140.3 chose
the smaller claim deliberately (decision mimid-1wgh.143).
